verdict.rationale: Honeybadger documents some first-party noise controls: grouping and deduplication of identical errors (a user specifically praises the deduping), and choosing which error events trigger a notification or ticket. That loosely covers the mute/ignore part of the story. Nothing in the evidence documents spike protection, per-key or per-error rate limits, or explicit mute/ignore rules for a bad deploy; the threshold alarms and anomaly detection create alerts rather than suppress them. missing for 10: spike protection, per-key rate limiting of notifications, explicit mute/ignore/snooze rules, independent corroboration of alert-fatigue handling
